dhp92:6: Rig Veda 1.25.7 says that Varuṇa “knows the track of birds flying through the midspace”.
dhp94:1: Similar imagery is found at Kaṭha Upaniṣad 3.3–9.
dhp97:1: This playful verse deploys a series of paradoxes not easy to convey in translation. | “Faithless” (_asaddho_): one who knows has no further need for faith ([sn41.8:2.1]()). | “Acknowledging nothing”: the Pali _akataññū_ resolves to “not-done-knower”. Normally it would mean “one who does not acknowledge what has been done for one”, translated as “ungrateful”. But if we construe the negative with “done” rather than “knower” it becomes, “knower of what was not made”, i.e. one who has realized Nibbana.
dhp97:2: _Sandhi_ is a connection or conjunction, here understood as the walls of a house (commentary; same sense also at Arthaśāstra 4.11.19, 7.17.48). A burglar “breaks into” a house, while the arahant “breaks out” of confinement in transmigration. _Sandhi_ suggests the “relinking (_paṭisandhi_) consciousness” of later Abhidhamma, the connection from one life to the next that is severed by the arahant, as well as the “house-builder” of [dhp153]()–4.
dhp97:3: _Avakāsa_ is an opportunity, often framed as the great opportunity for one fortunate enough to be reborn during the Buddha’s dispensation. An arahant “lacks prospects” since they have destroyed (_hata_) the seed for future rebirth.
